style.vernacular: Danube-Sava city of layered styles: pastel-rendered Central European neoclassical and Secession apartment blocks (ochre, cream, pale grey) with tall hipped roofs of terracotta tile; Zemun's Austrian Baroque low houses and bell-towered single-nave churches; interwar modernist and Art Deco blocks; and vast grey concrete socialist-modernist and brutalist slab blocks in Novi Beograd, with later glass offices and malls. Serbian Orthodox churches in stone and brick with domes.
style.ornament: Secession and Neo-Renaissance plaster ornament (garlands, cornices, caryatids) on city-centre facades; Neo-Byzantine bands of alternating stone and brick, small domes and a lantern on Orthodox churches; Zemun Baroque bell towers; prefabricated balcony bands and modular facades on Novi Beograd blocks; tall poplars, lime and plane trees along boulevards.

sources.what: Ottoman, neoclassical, Secession, Byzantine Revival, interwar modernism and Art Deco, socialist modernism/brutalist Novi Beograd blocks, Zemun Baroque churches
Prince Michael statue, National Museum/Theatre, dark cobble paving, plane trees
continental humid-subtropical climate; 19th-century Balkan/neoclassical/eclectic phases
